title: DOM XSS via Open Redirect
summary: A polished storefront's post-login loader trusts user-controlled query parameters and writes them straight into the DOM — chain an open redirect into DOM-based XSS.
vulnType: DOM-based XSS (chained from an open redirect)
author: Ovawatch Security
brief:
**Northstar Store** is a session-authenticated storefront. After certain actions it sends the browser through a `/loader` page that takes three query parameters — `next`, `bannerText`, and `timeoutDuration` — and uses them to show a friendly "redirecting" message before forwarding the user on.

The loader's client-side script reads those parameters and renders them **without sanitization**. Your job is to find the sink and prove both an open redirect and DOM-based XSS.

> Local, intentionally-vulnerable app. Use it only on your own machine.
objectives: Locate the loader page and identify which query parameters it consumes.
Find the DOM sink where untrusted input reaches the page.
Prove an open redirect to an external origin.
Escalate to DOM-based XSS that executes in the lab's origin.
Describe the root cause and a correct fix.

hints.text: Open the lab, then browse to /loader and watch what it does with the URL's query string.
View source on /loader. The inline script assigns to element.innerHTML using values taken directly from URLSearchParams.
bannerText is interpolated into innerHTML. HTML that triggers a load error event will run script without needing a <script> tag.
next controls window.location.href — point it at an external origin to demonstrate the open redirect.

solution: ## Root cause `public/loader.html` reads `next`, `bannerText`, and `timeoutDuration` from the query string and assigns them into the DOM via `innerHTML`, then sets `window.location.href = next`. ```js const next = params.get('next') || '/'; const bannerText = params.get('bannerText') || next; document.getElementById('redirect-message').innerHTML = `You are being redirected to ${bannerText}.`; window.location.href = next + '?utm_source=' + utm_source; ``` ## Open redirect ```text /loader?next=https://example.org ``` After the timeout the browser is sent to the attacker-chosen origin. ## DOM-based XSS `bannerText` is interpolated into `innerHTML`, so a tag with an error handler executes immediately: ```text /loader?bannerText= ``` A single crafted link gives an attacker script execution in the store's origin (session/cookie theft, account actions, etc.). ## Fix direction - Never assign untrusted input to `innerHTML`. Use `textContent` for the message. - Validate `next` against an allow-list of internal paths (reject absolute URLs and schemes like `javascript:`). - Apply a Content-Security-Policy that forbids inline event handlers.
